newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan ex-president and aides fined $600,000. [CORRECTED 03:18 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan ex-president and aides fined $600,000. [CORRECTED 03:18 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the figure in the headline and first paragraph to $600,000 from $600 million.)
Venezuela's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered disgraced former President Carlos Andres Perez and four of his top aides to pay more than $600,000 in damages to the state for misuse of government funds.

The fine, the exact amount of which is $603,295 (corrects figure from $603.3), was in addition to the 28-month sentence Perez completed in September for misappropriation of $17 million from a secret security spending account, Supreme Court President Cecila Sosa told a news conference.

Perez' Interior Minister Alejandro Izaguirre, Presidential Secretariat Minister Reinaldo Figueredo and two other government officials implicated in the case would share the fine with Perez, Sosa said.
"This is no surprise at all ... We have three days to appeal and, of course, we will do," Perez told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
Perez, 73, became the first Latin American leader to be convicted of corruption in May 1996, two years after the charges forced him out of office.
Perez has maintained his innocence and launched a new political movement after completing his term under house arrest.
